samples.summary: Document/tab/cell ids are interpolated into request paths without `encodeURIComponent`, so a crafted id can traverse out of the workspace-scoped base URL
samples.evidence: `base` is `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` (http-client.ts:82-85) and every content/tab/cell method appends the caller-supplied id raw: `getDocContent` -> `/documents/${docId}/content` (:283), `putDocContent` (:289), `getSlidesContent` (:300), `getNoteContent` (:317), `deleteDocument` (:205), `listTabs`/`renameTab` (:330, :336), `getCell`/`setCell`/`deleteCell` (:345, :348, :354). Only `downloadFileDocument` encodes (:254). An attacker who controls the id an agent passes (e.g. a doc id copied from an untrusted listing or a prompt) supplies `../../../../auth/refresh` or `../../other-ws/documents/x`; the WHATWG URL parser normalises the `..` segments, so the CLI issues the authenticated request (Bearer token attached at :63-66) against a path outside the workspace the user selected — request-path injection / workspace confusion. Server-side authz still applies to the resolved route, which is why this is not an escalation, but the CLI's own workspace scoping is bypassable and `--dry-run`'s printed path no longer matches what is sent. Not introduced by this diff; the diff refactors the error handling immediately around these call sites (commands/docs.ts:193, notes.ts:145, slides.ts:151).

samples.summary: `forwardUpstreamError` still forwards every field of a server-controlled error body verbatim to stderr, which is the channel this CLI documents as agent-readable
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:104-107 prints `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` once `isErrorEnvelope` passes, and the guard only validates that `error.code` is a string — `error.message` and any sibling keys are unbounded, unvalidated server text (the new test at packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:63-67 pins that extra fields are preserved). Backend error messages routinely embed user-controlled values such as document titles, so a user who can name a document can plant arbitrary text (including instruction-shaped text) in the stderr stream that the README tells agents to parse and branch on — indirect prompt injection into the consumer, plus pass-through of any field the backend/proxy adds. Control characters are safe (JSON.stringify escapes <0x20, so no ANSI/terminal-escape injection). This change narrows the pre-existing surface (truthiness -> structural check) rather than widening it; the residual risk is that `message`/extras are still unbounded pass-through. Mitigation would be to forward only the known envelope keys, or to length-cap `message`.

samples.summary: Export pipelines fetch absolute image URLs taken from document content, giving a document author an SSRF-lite primitive from the exporting machine
samples.evidence: `createImageFetcher` (image-fetcher.ts:45-56) passes any `src` whose scheme matches `/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i` straight to `fetch` untouched (`resolveImageUrl`, :28), with no host allow-list and no private-address filter. `docs export` (commands/docs.ts:258) and `slides export` (commands/slides.ts:197) build this fetcher over `res.data` — content authored by whoever can edit the document. A collaborator embeds an image whose `src` is `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or an internal host; the victim's export run issues that request from inside their network, and the response bytes are embedded into the produced PDF/DOCX/PPTX, giving a read-back channel. No credentials are attached (documented at :39-43), which limits it. Pre-existing and untouched by this diff, which only changes the error branch immediately above these call sites.
